label: early original-phase w/d/c/0/e/b input after an r/l/y/p/digit-led prefix
explanation: Active almost only in the original-input phase (99% of mass), peaking at t=3 (t=2..5 hold about 95% of mass); never at t=0, and almost never at the delimiter or during copy. The current input token matters most: w (10x lift, 39% of mass), then d, c, 0, e, b, mostly on the token first occurrence. The prefix modulates whether it fires and how strongly: the strongest activations come when the sequence starts with r (6x lift) or with l/y/p/digits, and when r/l/y sit two steps back. Top examples are all r-initial sequences with w/d at steps 2-4. The same tokens after prefixes like o/a/n/x/h/u usually do not fire, so this looks like an additive mix of current-token and prefix-token contributions that no simple boolean captures. The predicate gets most of the mass but with low precision (F1 about 0.42 on dev).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: w, d, c, 0, e, b; least: p, y, l, r) and the first original token (most: r, p, l, y, 2, 1; least: e, c, d, w); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, t=3, t=4.
